Andy Roddick has never been one to hold back, and the former American star had a particularly entertaining take on the frustration boiling over at the Shanghai Masters. With Alexander Bublik smashing his racquet and Frances Tiafoe struggling to contain his anger after a tough defeat, Roddick had little sympathy for those who find such outbursts unacceptable.
 Speaking about the incidents, Roddick summed up the mood among players after the US Open with a blunt observation: "Post US Open, everyone just loses their s**t."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement MEGHAN MCCARTHY/PALM BEACH DAILY NEWS / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images
 Andy Roddick Has No Problem With Bublik's Outburst
 Bublik is no stranger to emotional outbursts, and his latest one in Shanghai gave Roddick plenty to talk about. The Kazakh repeatedly smashed his racquet, then turned his frustration toward a courtside cooler, striking it forcefully with his hand.
 Rather than condemning the display, Roddick appeared to appreciate the commitment.
 "Yeah, see, I like that. Get your money's worth. Don't do it once if you got six in the chamber," he said.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement There was, however, a limit to Roddick's amusement. When Bublik started kicking things, the former world No. 1 immediately warned him against taking that route.
 "Don't kick. You can break a toe. Don't hit. Don't bring your hands into it."
 For Roddick, breaking a racquet is one thing. Injuring yourself by kicking a bench or punching a hard object is another. His humor came with a practical warning: the equipment might survive the match, but a player's hand or foot might not survive the outburst.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bublik had beaten Brandon Nakashima 6-7(7), 6-3, 7-6(5), before falling to Alexander Zverev 7-6(6), 4-6, 7-6(1) in the round of 16. The tight matches provided plenty of tension, but it was his reaction that caught Roddick's attention.
 Roddick Relates to Frances Tiafoe's Frustration
 Frances Tiafoe offered another example after his three-set loss to Alejandro Davidovich Fokina, going down 7-6(4), 4-6, 7-6(6). Reacting to Tiafoe's frustration, Roddick returned to his rule about keeping your hands and feet away from anything that could hurt you.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "No kicking benches. No kicking things that could win against your toe. No hitting things that can win against your hand. Breaking racquets… I don't care. I think it's funny."
 Roddick knows that view will not sit well with every tennis traditionalist. Some see racquet smashing as poor sportsmanship, but he admitted that the sight has never bothered him.
 "I'm like, yeah, I know, I know… it just doesn't bother me and I always find it funny and I laugh every time I see it. Maybe it's just because I have been there. I have done what they've done. I have broken rackets while they're still inside the bag that they got strung in."
